clue.text: Cunningly hides under a gun a lot of old gold pieces

definitions.text: a lot of old gold pieces
definitions.note: the phrase describes a large sum in former gold coins, plural like the answer

indicators.note: done cunningly, the letters of the words that follow are craftily rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone slyly stashes a fortune in old gold coins beneath a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cunningly' rearranges the fourteen letters of HIDES UNDER A GUN. A guinea was an old British gold coin worth 21 shillings; a hundred of them was a large sum.
explanation.definitionFit: The guinea was a British gold coin, so a hundred of them is plenty of old gold money.

clue.text: Old Greek infantryman I help to sort out

indicators.note: sorting out a jumble means rearranging the letters of the words just before

explanation.surface: A helper offers to tidy up after an ancient Greek foot soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavily armed foot soldier of ancient Greek city-states went by this name.

clue.text: A criminal record .

parts.note: read not as one person's convictions but as a published chronicle of crimes and executions at a famous London prison

explanation.walkthrough: Newgate was London's notorious old prison; its calendar was a popular eighteenth- and nineteenth-century collection of accounts of its criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: This publication literally recorded the lives and crimes of convicts held at Newgate gaol.

clue.text: … of uncommon excellence that is not often seen

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links it to the clue before but adds nothing to the parse; 'that is' joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is exceptionally fine, as a rare talent; the other is seldom encountered, as a rare bird.

clue.text: If cited thus the embezzler might have to explain it

definitions.text: If cited thus the embezzler might have to explain it

indicators.note: thus here means put in this other way, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An embezzler named in court would have to account for the missing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thus' rearranges IF CITED; read whole, the clue also describes the shortfall an embezzler leaves behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall in the accounts is what a thieving clerk would be asked to explain.

clue.text: See 1
It's hell for non-Gentiles when he gets in information on an uprising

indicators.note: he gets in means the word he goes inside the other piece

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising reads the little word an from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A remark on hell in Jewish tradition, framed around a report of a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets in' puts HE inside GEN, and 'uprising' turns AN into NA in this down clue. 'It's' and 'when', 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jewish and Christian scripture this valley outside Jerusalem became a name for the place of damnation.

clue.text: Politician I ring twice about African troops

indicators.note: to ring something is to surround it, so the pair of letters encloses the politician
twice means the single letter is written two times

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is the standard politician

explanation.surface: An MP describes phoning someone a second time about soldiers in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles I; 'ring' puts the pair round MP, and 'about' only reinforces the surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zulu regiment of warriors was called an impi.

clue.text: Beauty sleep that maybe taken as an alternative to redundancy?

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the words as early retiring to bed; the second is leaving a job early, sometimes offered to staff instead of making them redundant.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to bed early is the proverbial beauty sleep; leaving work before pension age is offered instead of being laid off.

clue.text: A place that isn't licensed to serve drinks

definitions.text: A place that isn't licensed to serve drinks

parts.words: A place that isn't licensed to serve drinks
parts.note: describes an unlicensed drinking den of the kind found in Ireland and South Africa, which sells alcohol anyway

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a café or teashop that serves no alcohol; the real sense is an illicit bar that serves it without a licence.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish and South African word for an illegal drinking house operating without a liquor licence.

clue.text: What one can do with money?

definitions.text: What one can do with money?

parts.words: What one can do with money?
parts.note: reads as what cash lets someone achieve, the influence that control of funds gives

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase usually means a legislature's control of public spending; here it is read as the clout money brings.
explanation.definitionFit: Control of finances gives influence, and this phrase names that financial leverage.

clue.text: I'm a man without an official position in Moslem society

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: without signals that the word an is removed from the word before it

parts.note: taken as written before the deletion
the two letters to remove

explanation.surface: Someone explains they hold no office in their Muslim community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes AN out of MAN, leaving M after IM and A. The definition stretches to the person who holds the post.
explanation.definitionFit: The prayer leader of a mosque, or a Muslim community leader, holds this title.

clue.text: Suetonius found them revolting!

parts.note: the Roman governor Suetonius Paulinus faced an uprising by a British tribe, so they were revolting in the sense of rebelling, not disgusting

explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like disgust; it means in revolt. Suetonius Paulinus crushed Boudicca's tribe in AD 60-61.
explanation.definitionFit: Boudicca's East Anglian tribe rose against Roman rule while Suetonius Paulinus governed Britain.

clue.text: Little king in extra neat residence

indicators.note: in places the abbreviated king inside the other piece

parts.note: a bye is an extra run in cricket
R, short for Latin rex, is the abbreviated king

explanation.surface: A small monarch lives in a very tidy house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is an old word for cattle, not tidy. A bye is a run scored in cricket without the batsman hitting the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowshed is where cattle, once called neat, are housed.

clue.text: Compere holding a party for a former Prince of Wales

indicators.note: holding means the compere's letters go round the other pieces

parts.note: MC, master of ceremonies, is a compere
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A host throws a party in honour of an old Welsh royal.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary Welsh prince said to have sailed to America centuries before Columbus.

clue.text: A tax haven for Polynesian traders?

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

explanation.surface: A Pacific island offering tax breaks to local merchants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax haven' wants to be read together; the definition is 'haven for Polynesian traders', a coral island harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped coral reef round a lagoon gives shelter to Pacific islanders' boats.

clue.text: Graceful insect introduced with wild glee

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of the word next to it are running riot into a new order

parts.note: an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An elegant bug arrives amid great merriment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges GLEE into ELEG; 'introduced with' joins it to ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish and refined in movement or look.

clue.text: The hunter who saw far too much of 22!

definitions.text: The hunter who saw far too much of 22!

parts.words: The hunter who saw far too much of 22!
parts.note: the mythical hunter came upon the goddess at 22 bathing naked and saw too much of her, and was turned into a stag

explanation.walkthrough: 'Far too much' means seeing her naked; for it the goddess changed him into a stag torn apart by his own hounds.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this huntsman glimpsed the chaste goddess bathing and was punished.

clue.text: An oil organisation in Pennsylvania providing musical entertainment

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania

indicators.note: organisation means the letters of the words before are reorganised

explanation.surface: An oil company in Pennsylvania sponsors a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' rearranges AN OIL into IANOL, and 'in' puts that inside PA. The definition is a self-playing piano, a source of musical entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanical player piano worked by perforated paper rolls entertained households.

clue.text: A bird enclosure covered with a firearm

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals

indicators.note: covered with means the firearm's letters surround the single letter

parts.note: a gun is a firearm
a means one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A bird's cage is draped with a shotgun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered with' puts I (a = one = I) inside GUN, after PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A flightless black-and-white seabird of the southern hemisphere.

clue.text: Severance pay awarded after failure to achieve union of agreement

definitions.text: Severance pay awarded after failure to achieve union of agreement

parts.words: Severance pay awarded after failure to achieve union of agreement
parts.note: 'severance' and 'union' suggest a job and trade unions, but the union is a marriage and the payment follows divorce

explanation.walkthrough: The industrial vocabulary misleads: the broken union is a marriage, and the court-ordered pay goes to the former spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Maintenance paid to an ex-spouse after a marriage breaks down.

clue.text: Metal state will take a hundred and one with hesitation

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one
um is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A US state hesitantly agrees to take in a hundred and one of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft silvery-white metallic element found in bones and chalk.

clue.text: Firm and clean reconditioned hide

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: something reconditioned is reworked, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A company offers to clean and restore an animal skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a noun, an animal skin; it is the verb. 'reconditioned' rearranges CLEAN into NCEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something out of sight.

clue.text: A scholar given special authority to travel by car round Northern Ireland

indicators.note: round means the driving word goes round the two-letter abbreviation

parts.note: to motor is to drive

explanation.surface: A privileged student is allowed to drive around Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a monitor is a pupil given duties of authority over others.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil appointed to help keep order or perform duties for teachers.

clue.text: Opponents of democratic measures

parts.note: reads as enemies of democracy, but means the people voting against a motion in a parliamentary division

explanation.walkthrough: Not anti-democrats: in a vote the ayes are for a measure and these are against it.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes, or voters, against a proposal in a legislature.

clue.text: A big noise going round with a very chaste female

indicators.note: going round means the noise's letters enclose the first letter-word

parts.note: a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A loud racket surrounds a most virtuous woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts the first A inside DIN; 'with' adds the second A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman virgin goddess of the hunt was a byword for chastity.

clue.text: Low average

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is base or petty; the other is the arithmetic midpoint of a set of numbers.

clue.text: Loose reef-knot

indicators.note: to knot is to tangle, so the letters of the word before get tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A sailor's reef knot that has come undone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reef-knot' reads as one sailing term; split, 'knot' tangles REEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconfined or untied, at liberty.

clue.text: A smack washed up on a beach, maybe

definitions.text: washed up on a beach, maybe

explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' means a taste, not a blow; the second sense is a kind of seaweed, called tang, found washed up on beaches.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a sharp taste or flavour; the other is seaweed of the kind thrown up on the shore.

clue.text: A spy holding up his umbrella?

definitions.text: A spy holding up his umbrella?

parts.words: A spy holding up his umbrella?
parts.note: a secret operative is pictured literally sheltering beneath his umbrella

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a spy operating in disguise is taken literally: someone under a cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret operative working under a false identity.

clue.text: Playroom that could be a handicap for two-year-olds of course

explanation.walkthrough: In British horse racing a nursery is a handicap race for two-year-olds; 'of course' points to a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a children's room; the other is a horse race with weights set for two-year-old horses.

clue.text: Obtainable from the girl at the tobacconist's shop?

definitions.text: Obtainable from the girl at the tobacconist's shop?

parts.words: Obtainable from the girl at the tobacconist's shop?
parts.note: suggests an item bought from the shop assistant, a device for smokers to ignite a cigarette

explanation.walkthrough: A tobacconist sells smokers' goods, including small devices for igniting cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pocket device that makes a flame for cigarettes, sold where tobacco is.
